title: Seller Performance Standing — Policy Violations and Violation Points
content:
**Clauses in force.**

1. Each recorded policy violation adds the points of its type from the violation points map.
2. An intellectual property violation is reversed in full when the rights owner retracts the complaint.
3. A violation is reversed when an appeal on the basis "violation issued in error" is accepted; an accepted plan of action appeal reinstates the seller but keeps the points on record until they expire.

## How violation points stand on the record

A seller's active violation points under Seller Performance Standing are a running total on the standing record: the points of each recorded violation come in, and every reversal and every points-expiry entry takes points out. Each violation is recorded with its own violation reference, its type, the listing concerned, the date recorded and the points recorded. A reversal is recorded against the violation reversed, with the points removed and the reason for the reversal; a points-expiry entry is recorded against the violation whose points it takes off, with the points removed.

| Event | Effect on active violation points |
|---|---|
| A policy violation is recorded | rises by the points of its type |
| An intellectual property violation's complaint is retracted by the rights owner | the violation is reversed in full; its points come out |
| An appeal on the basis "violation issued in error" is accepted | the violation is reversed; its points come out |
| A plan of action appeal is accepted | the seller is reinstated; the points stay on record until they expire |

## Retired clauses

The following two clauses of this policy are **no longer in force**. They have been superseded by the current basis and are not applied; they are kept here so that the record of the policy is complete.

> Points expire when the point expiry period has passed, counted in calendar days from the violation's event date.

As written, this clause ran the point expiry period in calendar days from the date the violation was recorded and treated the points as expired only once that period had passed. It is no longer in force.

> A reversed or expired violation is never reversed or expired a second time.

This clause is likewise no longer in force.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- A seller has one intellectual property violation and one listing policy violation on record. The rights owner retracts the intellectual property complaint: that violation is reversed in full and only the listing policy violation's points remain active.
- A suspended seller's plan of action appeal is accepted: the seller is reinstated, and the points of the violations remain on the record.
